entries.summary: Access log in combined format records client IP addresses and full request URLs, including query strings.
entries.rationale: morgan combined format (server.ts L370) writes remote address and the full request URL to logs/access.log, rotated daily (L361-369). IP addresses are Personal Data Elements. Query strings carry Personal Data and Authentication Secrets (see REF-028 and REF-029).

entries.summary: Card number stored in clear as an INTEGER column.
entries.rationale: cardNum is defined as DataTypes.INTEGER with range validators only. The full card number (Financial Data) is written to the Cards table without encryption or tokenisation. Responses show only the last four digits (routes/payment.ts L31-32), which does not change at-rest storage.

entries.summary: TOTP shared secret stored in plaintext in the Users table.
entries.rationale: totpSecret is a plain STRING column defaulting to an empty string, with no setter, encryption or hashing. The TOTP seed is an Authentication Secret, so a database read yields every second factor.

entries.summary: Account password stored as unsalted MD5.
entries.rationale: The password setter stores security.hash(clearTextPassword) at L73. security.hash is MD5 with no salt or work factor (lib/insecurity.ts L41). An Authentication Secret is hashed with a fast, unsalted function.

entries.summary: Security answers stored as HMAC output under a constant key shipped in the source.
entries.rationale: The answer setter stores security.hmac(answer) at L45. The HMAC key is a constant in lib/insecurity.ts (L42; value not reproduced). Low-entropy answers under a key that ships with the source give a deterministic, offline-guessable value. Judgement: treated as weak hashing of an Authentication Secret.

entries.summary: Login compares an MD5 digest of the submitted password inside a raw SQL query.
entries.rationale: The query interpolates the email and security.hash(password) into SELECT * FROM Users. The MD5 comparison is the weak-hashing point. The SQL injection on the same line is out of catalogue and recorded in the README. The SELECT * result feeds the JWT payload (REF-025).

entries.summary: RSA private key used to sign session tokens is hard-coded in source.
entries.rationale: The key defined at L21 is used by authorize() (L54) to sign session JWTs whose payloads carry Personal Data (email, role and the user record). Key material is not reproduced here. Anyone with the source can mint tokens for any Data Principal.

entries.summary: HMAC key protecting security answers is hard-coded in source.
entries.rationale: The key defined at L42 is used by security.hmac() for the security answers in models/securityAnswer.ts L45 (see REF-005). Value not reproduced here.

entries.summary: Error handler mounted without an environment guard; whether Personal Data reaches clients is not established.
entries.rationale: errorhandler() is mounted unconditionally (L722). Its output depends on NODE_ENV. Login SQL errors can contain the submitted email and password hash (routes/login.ts L34, REF-006).
entries.reason: The middleware output in the deployed NODE_ENV was not run. Code alone does not settle whether stack traces or Personal Data reach clients.

entries.summary: Any logged-in user can list and read every User record through the REST resource.
entries.rationale: GET /api/Users (L395) is guarded only by security.isAuthorized(). GET /api/Users/:id (L397) is guarded the same way. There is no ownership check, so any Data Principal reads other users' email, role, lastLoginIp and profileImage.

entries.summary: Any logged-in user receives every User row from the authentication-details endpoint.
entries.rationale: UserModel.findAll() runs with no filter and the rows are returned. The route is registered at server.ts L640. The only guard is session-level (L430), so no ownership check applies.

entries.summary: Complaint list returned to any logged-in user.
entries.rationale: GET /api/Complaints is guarded only by security.isAuthorized(). Complaint records carry UserId (models/complaint.ts L19) and a free-text message (L21). Single-record reads are denied at L415; the list route is not.

entries.summary: Recycle record read by id with no ownership check and no authentication.
entries.rationale: getRecycleItem runs RecycleModel.findAll filtered only by the id from the URL. server.ts L420 registers GET /api/Recycles/:id without a guard, so any caller reads other users' recycle records (UserId, AddressId, dates).

entries.summary: Memories endpoint is unauthenticated and returns every user's memories.
entries.rationale: GET /rest/memories is registered with getMemories() and no guard. The response includes UserId, image paths and captions for all users. The nested User rows are covered by REF-022.

entries.summary: Order history keyed on a vowel-masked email, so accounts with matching masked keys see each other's orders.
entries.rationale: Vowels in the email are replaced with asterisks and ordersCollection is queried with that value. Orders carry no user identifier, so two accounts whose emails differ only in vowels receive each other's orders.

entries.summary: Data export includes other Data Principals' orders through the same masked-email key.
entries.rationale: L22 applies the same vowel masking as orderHistory.ts and L33 queries ordersCollection with it. The export can therefore include orders belonging to another account (REF-015).

entries.summary: Invoice PDF with the customer's unmasked email is written into the public ftp/ folder.
entries.rationale: L45 writes order_<id>.pdf into ftp/. L65 prints the customer's full email in the document, while the order record stores a masked email (L170). ftp/ is published without authentication (REF-018).

entries.summary: ftp/ folder listing and file download are public, so invoices can be downloaded by anyone.
entries.rationale: ftp/ is served with directory listing (serve-index, icons) and a file route, with no authentication guard. Invoices written by routes/order.ts (REF-017) are therefore downloadable without a session.

entries.summary: Access-log directory and files are served without authentication.
entries.rationale: /support/logs is served with serve-index and serveLogFiles() on /support/logs/:file, with no authentication guard. The served access log contains client IP addresses and URLs with query strings (REF-001).

entries.summary: Unauthenticated order tracking returns order records holding a masked email and an address identifier.
entries.rationale: The route has no guard. L18 looks up the path id and L24 returns matching documents with a vowel-masked email and addressId. Order ids include a four-character MD5 prefix of the email (routes/order.ts L38-40). The NoSQL $where injection at L18 is out of catalogue.
entries.reason: Whether the masked email and addressId identify a Data Principal, and whether order ids are guessable, are judgements that code alone does not settle.

entries.summary: Authentication-details response spreads the full user record to the caller.
entries.rationale: The block returns ...user.dataValues. Email, role, deluxeToken, lastLoginIp and profileImage are returned unmasked. Password and totpSecret pass through a masking step in the same block; the remaining fields are returned as stored.

entries.summary: Memories query returns each owner's full user row, including password hash and TOTP secret.
entries.rationale: MemoryModel.findAll({ include: [UserModel] }) has no attributes filter. The nested User rows include email, password hash and totpSecret. The route is reached without authentication through server.ts L670 (REF-014).

entries.summary: User REST resource excludes only password and totpSecret.
entries.rationale: The finale User resource sets exclude to password and totpSecret only. Email, role, lastLoginIp, profileImage and deluxeToken still reach any logged-in caller through the list and read routes (L395-397, REF-010).

entries.summary: whoami fields parameter returns any stored user attribute, including password hash and TOTP secret.
entries.rationale: Every requested field is copied from the session user record into the response with no allow-list. Requesting password or totpSecret returns them. Lead passwordHashLeakChallenge is checked at L52.

entries.summary: Session JWT payload carries the full user row, including password hash and TOTP secret.
entries.rationale: authenticatedUser is set to { data: user, bid }, where user is the SELECT * row from L34 with all columns. L24 signs it with security.authorize (lib/insecurity.ts L54). JWT payloads are encoded, not encrypted. [INFERENCE] Any holder of the token can read the row. Established from the code path only; no token was decoded.

entries.summary: Save-login-IP endpoint returns the full updated user row to the caller.
entries.rationale: L32 updates lastLoginIp on the logged-in user. L33 calls res.json(updatedUser), which sends the whole model instance, including password hash and totpSecret. Registered at server.ts L658.

entries.summary: Public product reviews expose reviewer and liker email addresses.
entries.rationale: Review documents with author and likedBy (email addresses) are returned to any caller. server.ts L672 registers the route without a guard. The $where query at L36 is out of catalogue and recorded in the README.

entries.summary: Current, new and repeated passwords are read from the GET query string.
entries.rationale: query.current, query.new and query.repeat are read from the URL. The route is GET /rest/user/change-password (server.ts L636). Query strings are written to the access log (REF-001) and served publicly (REF-019).

entries.summary: Account email is read from the URL in the security-question lookup, without authentication.
entries.rationale: query.email is read from the URL and the account's security question is returned. The route is registered without a guard (server.ts L638). The response also reveals whether an account exists.

entries.summary: Session JWT stored in localStorage after login.
entries.rationale: authentication.token is written to localStorage. The payload carries the user record (REF-025), so Personal Data sits in browser storage that any script in the origin can read.

entries.summary: Email address stored in localStorage when remember-me is ticked.
entries.rationale: user.email is written to localStorage under the key email.

entries.summary: OAuth login stores the session JWT in localStorage.
entries.rationale: authentication.token is written to localStorage (same mechanism as REF-030).

entries.summary: Two-factor login stores the session JWT in localStorage.
entries.rationale: authentication.token is written to localStorage (same mechanism as REF-030).

entries.summary: Payment flow stores the session JWT in localStorage.
entries.rationale: data.token is written to localStorage (same mechanism as REF-030).

entries.summary: CORS wildcard applied to every route, including Personal Data routes.
entries.rationale: L184 answers preflight for all paths and L185 mounts cors() with the default Access-Control-Allow-Origin of '*' for all routes, including /api/Users, /rest/user/whoami and /profile.

entries.summary: Session token cookie set without HttpOnly, Secure or SameSite attributes.
entries.rationale: L192 calls res.cookie('token', token) with no options. Without HttpOnly, page scripts can read the token. Without Secure it travels over plaintext HTTP (REF-038). SameSite is left to browser defaults.

entries.summary: Whoami answers JSONP callbacks, returning Personal Data to cross-origin scripts.
entries.rationale: res.jsonp is used when a callback query parameter is present. The response carries id, email, lastLoginIp and profileImage (L36-41), or any field requested through fields (REF-024). JSONP lets any origin read the response, bypassing the same-origin policy.

entries.summary: HTTP listener on port 80 forwards to the application with no redirect to HTTPS.
entries.rationale: aws_lb_listener.http on port 80 has a forward default action. No redirect action exists in either Terraform tree. Port 80 accepts 0.0.0.0/0 (L69-72), so Personal Data sent to the application can travel in plaintext.

entries.summary: Same plaintext HTTP forward in the infrastructure Terraform tree.
entries.rationale: infrastructure/terraform/networking.tf is identical to terraform/networking.tf at this pin, so the same listener at L157-166 applies (REF-038).

entries.summary: Access-log retention of two days, below the one-year minimum for logs of Personal Data processing.
entries.rationale: Daily rotation is configured with max_logs set to 2d (L368). The access log carries Personal Data (REF-001). The SEC-13 row in docs/issue-types.md cites Rule 8(3) for one-year retention.

entries.summary: Persistent application data volume (EFS) has no backup in the terraform/ tree.
entries.rationale: The task mounts aws_efs_file_system.juice_shop_data (networking.tf L249) as its persistent volume. A repo-wide search for aws_backup in terraform/ and infrastructure/terraform/ returned no matches, so no backup plan or vault is configured.

entries.summary: Same unbacked EFS data volume in the infrastructure Terraform tree.
entries.rationale: infrastructure/terraform/main.tf mounts the same EFS file system, and that tree has no aws_backup resource either (REF-041).

entries.summary: LLM model provider receives Personal Data, but no consent withdrawal path exists to propagate.
entries.rationale: The stream call sends the system prompt (which carries the username, L201) and the chat messages to the configured model provider. The gate 'a Data Processor receives Personal Data' is met, but CON-05 presupposes a consent withdrawal that this code never records.
entries.reason: The gate is met, but the consent-withdrawal control that the Issue Type presupposes is absent. Whether this counts as a finding is a judgement.

entries.summary: Access-log events are written with no alerting or review in the repository.
entries.rationale: Access logs are written to files, including login and password-related requests. The in-repo monitoring config (monitoring/grafana-dashboard.json) covers challenge progress only. Neither Terraform tree contains an alarm, metric filter or alert rule.

entries.summary: User rows are soft-deleted and kept, so erased Personal Data stays stored.
entries.rationale: paranoid is set to true (L120), so a destroy only marks the row and keeps it. No route deletes User rows: DELETE /api/Users/:id is denied (server.ts L399). Personal Data and Authentication Secrets therefore remain after an erasure request (REF-046).

entries.summary: Erasure request only sets a flag; no code consumes it and no data is erased.
entries.rationale: A privacy-request row is created with deletionRequested set to true, and the route returns. Nothing outside this route reads that flag (checked across routes, models, lib and server.ts). The user's rows remain.

entries.summary: Data export omits categories of Personal Data held about the user.
entries.rationale: userData is built from username, email, memories, orders and reviews only. It omits address records, card records, lastLoginIp, profileImage, complaints, feedback, recycle requests, wallet and deluxe status. Complaints, feedback and recycles each carry UserId (models/complaint.ts L19, models/feedback.ts L23, models/recycle.ts L20).

entries.summary: No route corrects the user's email; PUT and DELETE on the user record are denied.
entries.rationale: PUT and DELETE on /api/Users/:id are denied (L398-399). The only profile write (routes/updateUserProfile.ts L38) changes username. Email, which the user sees in whoami (routes/currentUser.ts L38), has no correction route.

entries.summary: Privacy notice lists no Data Principal rights; the nomination check cannot be applied.
entries.rationale: A contact email is given under Contact Us (L164-167). No section lists Data Principal rights, correction, erasure, grievance redress or nomination.
entries.reason: RIG-04's gate needs an in-repo notice that lists rights under the DPDP Act. This notice lists none, so the outcome is not determinable under docs/issue-types.md.

entries.summary: Chat sends the username and messages to a model provider; whether the notice discloses this is a judgement.
entries.rationale: The username is read from the token (L193), the system prompt is built with it (L201), and the prompt and messages are sent to the model provider (L204-208). The endpoint is config llmApiUrl in config/default.yml, defaulting to http://localhost:11434/v1. The notice covers service providers only generically (privacy-policy component L128-132).
entries.reason: Whether the generic service-provider clause discloses this flow, and whether the configured endpoint is external, are judgements that code alone does not settle.

entries.summary: Application region defaults to eu-west-1, so the persistent Personal Data store is held outside India.
entries.rationale: aws_region defaults to eu-west-1. The provider (terraform/main.tf L2) and the EFS data volume (REF-041) use that region. Storage outside India meets the Issue Type condition. docs/issue-types.md marks the finding Needs Legal Review unless the destination is restricted under section 16; no restriction was found in the repo. Confirmed on the code fact; the legal characterisation is left to counsel.

entries.summary: Same eu-west-1 default in the infrastructure Terraform tree.
entries.rationale: infrastructure/terraform/variables.tf sets the same default (REF-051), so the same storage location applies.
